Many patients with breast cancer overproduce the protein HER2, which drives aggressive tumor growth. Therapies directed at HER2 have substantially extended survival; however, up to one-third of patients still experience spread to the brain, where management is particularly challenging. This review synthesizes evidence on the significant classes of HER2-targeted therapy—monoclonal antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates, and small-molecule inhibitors—highlighting survival outcomes and activity in the brain.
